title: Fleet lifecycle automation: predictive drains, staged upgrades, and maintenance windows
creator: Maya Chen
description: Implement an automated fleet lifecycle engine for Dedicated capacity that handles node-level draining, predictive preemptive drains, staged rolling upgrades, and configurable maintenance windows. This feature should ensure throughput guarantees and low-risk upgrades for customers using reserved pools. The work covers: (1) a decision engine that consumes telemetry (OOMs, GPU ECC errors, NVMe SMART, kernel panics, container restart rates) and flags nodes for predictive drains; (2) a scheduling system for maintenance windows and blackout periods per-fleet; (3) a staged upgrade flow with canary cohorts, circuit-breaker thresholds for traffic routing to preserve throughput SLA, and automated rollback on quality or latency regressions; (4) integration points with Console (maintenance calendar, audit trail) and runtime (graceful KV cache transfer, connection handoff); (5) observability hooks (traces, per-node drain metrics, upgrade histograms) and runbook links for SREs.
acceptance_criteria: Decision engine flags nodes for drain when a configurable combination of signals crosses thresholds and emits a drain plan in JSON that the scheduler can act on
Maintenance windows can be created per-fleet with timezone-aware recurrence, and fleet-wide blackout periods prevent upgrades/drains during critical customer windows
Staged upgrade workflow supports cohort size config, pre-upgrade canary tests, and automated traffic throttling to keep per-fleet throughput >= configured guarantee or trigger fallback routing
Graceful drain flow migrates KV cache and active connections where possible, with documented timeout behavior and metrics emitted for every drain operation
Console shows pending/planned drains and upgrades with audit events, and SRE can force-cancel or reschedule operations with RBAC checks
End-to-end e2e test covering a simulated node health failure causes predictive drain and capacity is restored via autoscaling or fallback pool without violating SLOs in a 30-minute window
comments: 2025-02-20 Maya Chen: Created ticket after architecture sync. Initial scope focused on predictive drains + maintenance windows. Suggested we tie decision thresholds to historical percentiles rather than fixed values.

2025-02-24 Arjun Patel: Spike complete — telemetry adapter prototype exists and can emit candidate-drain events. Found that NVMe SMART noise causes false positives; proposed median-filter + hysteresis in signal aggregation.

2025-02-28 SRE Review (Priya Nair): Recommended adding explicit circuit-breaker for throughput guarantees to avoid customer impact during large fleet upgrades. Added runbook step to escalate to on-call if rollback fails after 2 attempts.
2025-03-01 Design Review (Ethan Ruiz): Console mockups uploaded. UX shows maintenance calendar and single-click 'pause upgrades' action. Need to confirm audit log retention policy with Security.

2025-03-03 Arjun Patel: Implemented scheduler prototype. It supports timezone-aware recurrence and cohort sizing for staged upgrades. Integration tests failing intermittently due to kube drain timing — added exponential backoff and improved metric emission.

2025-03-05 Maya Chen: Product accepted planned scope; prioritizing predictive drain thresholds and staged upgrades for cycle 2025-W09. Next: security review, SLO test plan, and canary test harness implementation (ENG-15824 as child ticket).
2025-03-05 TODO: Add customer-facing docs and migration guide for fleets that previously relied on manual maintenance windows.
notes: Trade-offs discussed: aggressive preemptive drains reduce unplanned outages but increase churn and transient capacity pressure; solution chosen favors conservative thresholds with hysteresis and automated scaling fallback. We will monitor false-positive rate for 4 weeks post-launch and iterate thresholds.
qa_plan: Automated e2e test suite that simulates node failures (OOM, ECC, nvme) and validates drain + autoscale + traffic routing. Add load tests to assert throughput guarantees under cohort upgrades. Manual runbook validation with SRE before GA.
risks: Incorrect thresholds could cause unnecessary draining and increased cost; upgrade cohorts that are too small extend upgrade windows; rollback logic may leave degraded nodes in fleet if not fully validated.
mitigation: Add canary validation gates, gradual ramp-up of decision sensitivity, observability dashboards, and an opt-out per-customer flag for manual maintenance control.
